title: Serbian Cafe Offers Coffee with Alpacas
paragraphs: Cat cafes have become popular in many countries. But in Serbia, there is now a cafe where customers can enjoy their coffee with alpacas.

The Alpaca Cafe opened at the end of September 2026 at the Tiganjica Ethno-Village resort in Stajicevo, about 50 kilometers north of Belgrade, Serbia's capital city. In the cafe, six alpacas walk freely between the tables while visitors drink their coffee.
Alpacas are animals from South America. They have long necks and soft, thick wool, and they look a little like small llamas. They are not often seen in cafes in Europe.
A visit to the cafe costs about 10 euros. This includes a drink and a bucket of food to give to the alpacas. Visitors need to book in advance, and many people come on organized tours.

There are some rules for visitors. People should not walk up to the alpacas from behind, and they should not give the animals their own food. Instead, the cafe gives visitors buckets of carrots, lettuce and apples.

Each alpaca has its own personality. According to Simona Frangi, who takes care of the animals, Ljubica, a black alpaca, can be grumpy, and Snezana is the leader of the group even though she is the smallest. Frangi says alpacas are very sensitive to people's intentions.
The resort's owner, Zoran Ostojin, got the idea after visiting an alpaca cafe in Slovakia. Ostojin said the family wanted people in Serbia to get to know alpacas and feel their energy.

The resort, which also has a restaurant, a garden and a small zoo, received its first alpaca as a gift from the Belgrade Zoo eight years ago. Ostojin believes alpacas have an energy that is almost like a healing ability.
